questions.question: Work out 24 times 6 by breaking down, and explain how an estimate checks your answer.
questions.expected_answer: 24 is 20 plus 4. 6 times 20 is 120 and 6 times 4 is 24. Add: 120 plus 24 is 144. Estimate: 25 times 6 is 150, which is close to 144, so the answer is believable.

questions.question: Use the grid method to work out 23 times 14, naming all four partial products.
questions.expected_answer: Split 23 into 20 and 3 and 14 into 10 and 4. Products: 10 times 20 is 200, 10 times 3 is 30, 4 times 20 is 80, 4 times 3 is 12. Add: 200 plus 30 plus 80 plus 12 is 322.

questions.question: Work out 36 times 25 by the grid method and by a shortcut, and show that they agree.
questions.expected_answer: Grid: 20 times 30 is 600, 20 times 6 is 120, 5 times 30 is 150, 5 times 6 is 30; total 900. Shortcut: 36 is 4 times 9, 25 times 4 is 100, 100 times 9 is 900. Both give 900.
